news:adgon4$hpb$1...@dinkel.civ.utwente.nl...

> Can both be used at the same time ?
>
> Sander

Pounce:
Requires a ready minion with Flight. Strike: strength+2 damage, and the
opposing minion cannot strike for the remainder of the round (this doesn't
affect the current strike resolution). If this strike is dodged, this
striking minion takes 1 damage during strike resolution and the opposing
minion gets an optional press.

Definition of a hand strike:
And non ranged, non weapon strike, based on the user's strength.

Pounce is a hand strike and is legal to play when you've been grappled.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <c10e19afe1ccc095cc2...@mygate.mailgate.org>,

Claus Staal <c...@mbureauet.dk> writes:
>> Hand strikes are strikes which:
>>
>> - do damage based on strength - CHECK
>> - close range strikes - CHECK
>> - not melee weapon strikes - CHECK
>
>So at the same token would Scorpion愀 Touch also be a Hand Strike??

If you choose to make a hand strike with Scorpion's Touch, yes. (You
might have chosen a melee weapon strike, per card text.)

Similarly, Undead Strength is a hand strike. Lucky Blow is a hand
strike. Scorpion Sting is a hand strike. The fallback of Compress
(pot) is a hand strike. The Khabar: Honor is a hand strike. Blissful
Agony (ani fallback) is a hand strike.

Thus, they would all (and plenty of other strikes) be playable under
Immortal Grapple.

Also, since hand strikes deal hand damage, they would all be subject to
Wolf Claws (or similar) too.



Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
vermillian wrote:

> And garotte is not?

Garrotte is a weapon. You can't use weapons while immortally grappled. Only
hand strikes.

Weapons are based on strength damage, but are not hand strikes, as they are
weapons. While Immotally Grappled, you may not use Brass Knuckles, Meat
Cleaver, Sengir Dagger, or anything that is a weapon. They aren't hand
strikes.

Pounce is not a weapon. It is based on strength damage. It is non ranged.
Thus, it is a hand strike.

Garrotte is a weapon. Thus it fails the "Is it a hand strike" test.


